reviews.title: Rating & Review of NeuroGym’s Innecise
reviews.text: Innercise has proven to be one of the most cost-effective investments I’ve made in myself. Not only does it offer valuable insights from NeuroGym's founder, John Assaraf, but it also exposes users to a variety of experts across diverse fields. Last October, I purchased a lifetime membership, and since then, I’ve been actively challenging my belief system, breaking bad habits one by one, and cultivating a mindset that enables me to achieve my goals without unnecessary stress. Backed by cutting-edge scientific and brain research, this program has supported my mindset training and mental fitness in ways that far exceeded my initial expectations. When I first heard the term "innercise," I scoffed, assuming it was merely a clever fusion of "inner" and "exercise"—likely something akin to raja yoga. I couldn’t have been more wrong. Innercise is not only practical but also scientifically grounded, fundamentally reshaping how I approach personal development. One of the most impactful tools I’ve encountered is the My Coach module. In a recent interaction, I shared exactly how I was feeling and requested guidance on suitable innercises. My coach not only recommended one of my favorite foundational innercises, Take Six: Calm the Circuits, but also provided additional strategies to address my concerns. This personalized approach has been incredibly insightful. As someone who has long struggled with procrastination—particularly when it comes to writing—this program has been a game-changer. I had been putting off writing a review of how valuable Innercise has been for me, despite my intention to do so weeks ago. However, after completing the A.I.A. Innercise today, I committed to writing this review within 24 hours—and here it is. In conclusion, Innercise has empowered me to take small, consistent steps toward becoming a better version of myself. It encourages me to observe and apply what I learn without harsh self-judgment, aligning perfectly with my personal philosophy. I look forward to continuing my journey with Innercise because it asks little of me but offers tremendous value in terms of personal growth.

reviews.title: Innercise Newbie
reviews.text:
Innercise is a great investment for the cost. It’s truly an excellent value. I’m still familiarizing myself with the app and figuring out how to obtain maximum benefits for my personal growth, development, to achieve dynamic goals and live my best life. The support team is very attentive. They genuinely care and respond promptly to inquiries. This personal touch is what sets them apart. In our robotic world, it really makes me feel like I’m part of a community and not just a number. John Aseraf has Q&A sessions and interacts with us in zoom meetings. I like the more social aspect that provides in a virtual group setting.
The app is evolving and since there’s always room to raise the bar a little higher, I know that the app will be outstanding in no time.

reviews.title: Good but needs improvements
reviews.text: I like this app and it is full of great mindset audios. There are a few things that could be improved. On my home screen it has certain audios that say general terms, ie “gratitude” I expect it to be a generic gratitude audio but it’s for sales. I can’t seem to find a general “gratitude “ audio and worse, I don’t know how to create a Home Screen that works for me. In addition, the search function is just an AI bot and it doesn’t help you find anything. I have been looking for an audio to help me sleep and it suggested something that I cannot find on the app. There are a lot of expert speakers, and specific programs ie losing weight, but I can’t seem to navigate through things effectively or efficiently. The other problem is the meditation music isn’t what it is labeled. Babbling brook is anything but that. Mountain zen isn’t what I expected, and desert calm(not sure that’s the correct title) doesn’t sound like the desert. I know because I lived in Arizona for over 30 years. YouTube has much better meditation music. Overall, I would give it an 8 because of all the material, but I wish I could get rid of the sales audios or hide them, and find what I’m looking for with the search function.
